security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, and relative documentation links. One command template can invoke a Resend connector to create and schedule broadcasts, and one user-derived output filename needs containment to prevent unintended file locations.

remediation.issue: The Resend command template can create and schedule email broadcasts.
remediation.suggestion: Keep preview and explicit confirmation mandatory, validate every argument, and require an explicit live flag immediately before the mutating command.

remediation.issue: The save path contains a user-derived flow-or-goal filename placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Convert the value to a restricted filename slug and verify the resolved path remains inside memory/email/email-sequence-designer before writing.

content.value_statement: Email programs can become inconsistent when triggers, cadence, and exit rules are not planned together. This skill creates a structured flow map with governance controls and a lifecycle score.
actual_capabilities: Maps welcome, cart, browse-abandon, post-purchase, re-engagement, and B2B outbound flows.
Defines triggers, delays, goals, branch logic, and exit conditions for each flow.
Sets send caps, quiet hours, and fatigue guardrails across lifecycle flows.
Designs a re-engagement and sunset path for declining engagement.
Calculates and annotates the SEND N dimension score for a selected profile.
Provides Resend command guidance with preview and user-confirmed live execution steps.
limitations: It does not write individual email subjects, bodies, or calls to action.
It does not calculate the final EQS or enforce unsubscribe vetoes.
It does not create closed-loop re-consent programs for lapsed cohorts.
It needs reliable trigger and segment details to produce an accurate enrollment design.

use_cases.title: Launch a welcome series
use_cases.description: Create an onboarding flow with signup triggers, timed steps, conversion exits, and a global cadence policy.

use_cases.title: Recover abandoned carts
use_cases.description: Plan a cart sequence with discount branches, purchase exits, and limits that prevent excessive contact.

use_cases.title: Reduce list fatigue
use_cases.description: Add re-engagement, throttling, and sunset rules to an existing lifecycle program.

prompt_templates.title: Start a welcome flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a welcome flow for [product] and [audience]. The signup trigger is [event]. Include three steps, timing, exits, and quiet hours.

prompt_templates.title: Build a cart recovery flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an abandoned-cart flow for [store]. Use [number] steps, a [discount] branch, exit on purchase, and a weekly send cap of [limit].

prompt_templates.title: Audit lifecycle coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these existing flows: [paste details]. Identify missing lifecycle stages and propose triggers, segments, cadence, and sunset rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a governed multi-flow program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design welcome, browse-abandon, post-purchase, and re-engagement flows for [audience]. Use the [profile] SEND N profile and provide score notes and open assumptions.

output_examples.input: Design a welcome flow for a trial software product.
output: Step 1: Send within 15 minutes with setup guidance.
Step 2: Send after two days if setup remains incomplete.
Exit: stop after paid conversion, unsubscribe, or hard bounce.
Governance: maximum two lifecycle emails in seven days.

output_examples.input: Create an abandoned-cart sequence with a discount branch.
output: Trigger: cart remains unpaid for one hour.
Step 2: Show product benefits after 24 hours without purchase.
Branch: offer a discount after 72 hours only to eligible segments.
Sunset: suppress after the final step or a completed purchase.

best_practices: Confirm the trigger event and eligible segment before setting enrollment rules.
Use explicit conversion, reply, unsubscribe, and bounce exits for every flow.
Set program-wide caps and quiet hours before adding more messages.
anti_patterns: Do not enroll suppressed or non-consented contacts.
Do not use a win-back flow when a formal re-consent program is required.
Do not treat estimated timing assumptions as measured performance data.

faq.question: Does this skill write the email copy?
faq.answer: No. It designs the flow structure. Use an email creative skill to write each message.

faq.question: Can it design an abandoned-cart sequence?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define timing, discount branches, purchase exits, and frequency controls.

faq.question: Can it send messages through an ESP?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for Resend commands. Live sending requires a preview and user confirmation.

faq.question: Does it handle consent records?
faq.answer: No. It relies on the consent registry and requires suppressed contacts to remain excluded.

faq.question: What is the SEND N score?
faq.answer: It is a lifecycle score covering flow coverage, timing, relevance, progression, and preference options.

faq.question: When should I use a reactivation skill instead?
faq.answer: Use it for a defined lapsed cohort that needs a closed-loop win-back or re-consent program.
